paper_title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
core_problem: Large language models have been increasingly used to interact with external environments as goal-driven agents, but it remains challenging for these language agents to quickly and efficiently learn from trial-and-error as traditional reinforcement learning methods require extensive training samples and expensive model fine-tuning.
methodology_summary: Reflexion is a framework to reinforce language agents not by updating weights but through linguistic feedback. Reflexion agents verbally reflect on task feedback signals and maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer to induce better decision-making in subsequent trials. The framework is flexible enough to incorporate various types, e.g., scalar values or free-form language, and sources, e.g., external or internally simulated, of feedback signals.
empirical_results: Reflexion obtains significant improvements over a baseline agent across diverse tasks including sequential decision-making, coding, and language reasoning. On HumanEval coding benchmark, Reflexion achieves 91% pass@1 accuracy, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GPT-4 that achieves 80%.
